text:
Morgan Frost has 14 points in 24 games for Calgary, a scoring rate a touch above the middle of his talent range. Six of those points have come on the power play, and that unit is doing a lot of the lifting for him right now.

At even strength the last ten games have been thin. He has five points, close to the 5.9 our numbers expected, but just 1.0 expected goals on his own shots against 2.1 usual, and the Flames have been outchanced at 5v5 with him on (47% of the expected goals). His goal at Los Angeles on Nov. 14 was his only one in that stretch.

The better version of Frost is in the data. Evolving-Hockey had him 73rd among 401 forwards last season, with weak teammates hiding some of his own effect, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking shows a transition player: he carries the puck in 61% of the time and 61% of his shots come off the rush. Calgary needs him getting those rush looks back.
headline: Morgan Frost's power play is carrying his line
